title: Ringed-topos pullback of a flat module sheaf
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C\prime$ be small sites, $\mathcal O,\mathcal O\prime$ sheaves of commutative rings on them, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C\prime)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ whose left adjoint preserves finite limits. Give a ring-sheaf homomorphism $c:u^{-1}\mathcal O\to\mathcal O\prime$. For a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], put $u^*F=u^{-1}F\otimes_{u^{-1}\mathcal O}\mathcal O\prime$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $F$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then $u^*F$ is a flat $\mathcal O\prime$-module sheaf. No flatness of $c$ is assumed. Tensor product is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and flat module sheaf is [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Apply inverse-image preservation of flatness to the algebraic inverse-image lift I and F. This proves that G=I.modules.obj F is flat over RI before the coefficient map c is applied.

The module-to-abelian-sheaf functor preserves finite colimits: apply the module sheafification adjunction to a diagram of underlying presheaves; the invertible counit identifies its sheafified diagram with the original one, and forgetting sheafification is abelian sheafification. It preserves and reflects finite limits and reflects finite colimits. Restriction of scalars has the same underlying abelian sheaf functor, hence preserves finite limits and colimits.

Use the natural scalar tensor comparison with M=G. The source comparison functor is restriction of scalars, followed by the exact tensor functor of G, followed by forgetting; it therefore preserves finite limits and colimits. Transfer these properties through the natural isomorphism and reflect them through forgetting on the S-module side. This proves IsFlatOnSite of changeOfRingsOfUniverses c G.

proof_origin.place: Tags 05VD and 05V4. M2 formalizes the full scalar-extension step using tensor descent through sheafification and exactness reflected on abelian sheaves; inverse-image flatness is isolated as the strictly smaller pre-scalar-extension step.
